summary: Boise NF summit log lookout: 1914 first cabin, CCC log house by 1929-30, staffed to 1995, burned in a lightning-started fire in 2002. Ruins in a 2019 photo.

facts.design: Two-story log house, 20 by 20 feet (replacement); the first lookout was an 18 by 18 foot two-story log house
facts.agency: Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association (lookout); Boise National Forest (land)
facts.status_note: Burned in 2002. A 2019 climbing guide photo is captioned as showing the ruins; no later source found.

access.note: On Boise National Forest land, reached by Forest Service roads described in a 2019 guide; the start of the approach crosses private land. No closure found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: The lookout burned and only ruins are recorded, so there is no standing structure to climb. A 2019 guide describes the road to the summit.

events.note: First lookout, a two-story 18 by 18 foot log house built by the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association

Replacement 20 by 20 foot log house built by a CCC crew under two Finnish carpenters. Sources give 1929 (NHLR build field, FFLOS, Forest Lookouts list), 1930 (Idaho Fire Lookouts) or the 1930s (NHLR text)
Staffed through the 1995 season, then decommissioned
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register; first Idaho log house on the list

Newspaper: timber association willing to sell for $1; a new East Mountain Lookout Committee to be part of the Central Idaho Cultural Center in McCall. firelookout.com says the Center had already bought it. Sources disagree
Fire started by a dry lightning storm in late June or early July 2002; burned the lookout down while a preservation group was restoring it
Climbing guide photo captioned 'The lookout ruins in 2019.'

corrections.current: 2001 burned (burned down; it had been counted among the lookouts eligible for the NRHP)
corrections.proposed: Remove the 2001 event. The fire year is 2002 (see the 2002 burned event).
corrections.why: Three of the four sources that date the fire give 2002. The 2001 date appears only in a 2006 chapter report, which reads as a slip about the same fire.

resolved_conflicts.field: build year of the replacement lookout
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR build field and FFLOS say 1929, and the Forest Lookouts list says 1929; Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1930; NHLR text says the 1930s. Record keeps 1929 with the disagreement noted.

resolved_conflicts.field: storeys of the lookout standing in 1997
resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1997 AP story calls the standing CCC-era lookout three-story. The Forest Lookouts list describes the 20 by 20 foot replacement as two-story, and NHLR and FFLOS describe the first lookout as two-story. The story uses two-story for the first lookout and gives the AP description.
7,723 ft (NHLR, FFLOS), 7,752 ft (AP 1997) and 7148 ft (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Record keeps the 2,354 m figure from NHLR.
The 1997 AP story says the timber association was willing to sell for $1; firelookout.com says the Cultural Center had purchased it. The story says the sources differ.
2002 (NHLR, firelookout.com, climbing guide) against 2001 (2006 chapter report). Story uses 2002.

notes_for_editor: Access is set to public from land ownership and the 2019 road description; no current access rule was found, so please confirm before publishing. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced. The brief's NHLR registration date (Aug 15, 1997) and FFLOS registration date (Jan 7, 2021) were not visible in the fetched text, so the record gives only the year (1997) and omits the 2021 FFLOS event. Status changed from gone to ruins, based on the 2019 caption only. No photos recorded: the NHLR photo credits give no licence.
